newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: No deal yet on EU ship aid, talks to continue.
newsitem.headline: No deal yet on EU ship aid, talks to continue.

text.p: European Union industry ministers were expected to continue tough talks later on Thursday to try to find an agreement on state aid to ailing shipyards in Germany, Greece and Spain.

There was not yet the necessary number of member states in favour of a proposal of the European Commission to approve the requests of Bonn, Athens and Madrid to grant the restructuring aid totalling some $1.56 billion, an EU official said.
"We do not yet have (a qualified majority)," he told reporters, adding that negotiations would continue but gave no prediction of the outcome.
Sweden and Finland had confirmed they could not agree to the proposal to clear the aid in the three countries while Britain had indicated it would abstain in a vote on the issue.
France, however, insisted to link its approval of the proposal to a separate agreement to extend existing EU ship aid rules for another two years.
The EU's so called seventh shipbuilding directive, which allows for contract related aid of up to nine percent, is due to expire by the end of this year and Paris wants to prolong it.
Other countries, such as the Nordics and Britain, are not willing to agree to such an extension, preferring instead to see a new EU aid regime with stricter rules for granting state support.

German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt confirmed that the issue of aid to German, Greek and Spanish yards was blocked for the moment because of the disagreement on whether to extend the shipbuilding directive but expressed optimism that there would be a deal in the end.
Luxembourg Economy Minister Robert Goebbels also expressed optimism about an agreement on both issues.

The debate on future ship aid rules comes against the background of continued failure of the United States to ratify an accord brokered within the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development to slash shipbuilding support.

If the United States does not ratify the deal, the EU needs to reach agreement on rules for handling shipbuilding subsidies to its yards, the only manufacturing industry in the bloc to still receive large amounts of operating aid.
